edition.copy_text: Koetschau, GCS 2–3 (1899), via the Perseus TEI

source_text: Ἐκ δὲ τῶν εἰρημένων τοῖς συνετώτερον ἀκούουσι δῆλον, πῶς ἀπαντητέον καὶ πρὸς τό· τὸ μὲν ἄλλο πᾶν ἐξοπτήσεσθαι γένος, αὐτοὺς δὲ μόνους διαμενεῖν. οὐ θαυμαστὸν δ᾿ εἰ τοιαῦτα νενόηκε „τὰ“ ἐν ἡμῖν ὑπὸ τοῦ λόγου „μωρὰ τοῦ κόσμου“ ὀνομαζόμενα καὶ „ἀγενῆ“ καὶ „ἐξουδενωμένα“ καὶ „μὴ ὄντα,“ ἅτινα „διὰ τῆς μωρίας τοῦ κηρύγματος εὐδόκησεν ὁ θεὸς σῶσαι τοὺς πιστεύοντας αὐτῷ, ἐπεὶ μὴ ἐν τῇ σοφίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ ἔγνω ὁ κόσμος διὰ τῆς σοφίας τὸν θεὸν,“ οὐ δυνάμενα διαρθρῶσαι τὰ κατὰ τοὺς τόπους οὐδὲ βουληθέντα σχολάσαι τῇ ἐρεύνῃ τῆς γραφῆς, καίτοι γε τοῦ Ἰησοῦ λέγοντος· „ἐρευνᾶτε τὰς γραφὰς,“ καὶ τοιαῦτα ὑπείληφε περὶ τοῦ ἐπαγομένου πυρὸς ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ περὶ τῶν συμβησομένων τοῖς ἁμαρτήσασι. καὶ τάχα ὥσπερ τοῖς παισὶν ἁρμόζει τινὰ λέγεσθαι κατάλληλα τῇ νηπιότητι αὐτῶν πρὸς τὸ ὡς παῖδας κομιδῇ νηπίους ἐπιστρέφειν αὐτοὺς ἐπὶ τὸ βέλτιον, οὕτως οἷς ὠνόμασεν ὁ λόγος μωροῖς τοῦ κόσμου καὶ ἀγενέσι καὶ ἐξουδενωμένοις ἡ πρόχειρος ἁρμόζει περὶ τῶν κολάσεων ἐκδοχὴ, οὐ χωροῦσιν ἄλλην ἢ τὴν διὰ φόβου καὶ φαντασίας τῶν κολάσεων ἐπιστροφὴν καὶ τῶν πολλῶν κακῶν ἀποχήν. ὁ λόγος οὖν μόνους μὲν ἀγεύστους τοῦ πυρὸς καὶ τῶν κολάσεών φησι διαμενεῖν τοὺς τὰ δόγματα καὶ τὰ ἤθη καὶ τὸ ἡγεμονικὸν ἄκρως κεκαθαρμένους· τοὺς δὲ μὴ τοιούτους, κατὰ τὴν ἀξίαν χρῄζοντας τῆς διὰ πυρὸς κολάσεως οἰκονομίας, ἐν τούτοις ἐπί τινι τέλει φησὶν ἔσεσθαι, ὃ τῷ θεῷ ἁρμόζει ἐπάγειν τοῖς „κατ᾿ εἰκόνα“ αὐτοῦ πεποιημένοις καὶ παρὰ τὸ βούλημα τῆς „κατ᾿ εἰκόνα“ φύσεως βεβιωκόσι. καὶ ταῦτα δὲ πρὸς τό· τὸ μὲν ἄλλο πᾶν ἐξοπτήσεσθαι γένος, αὐτοὺς δὲ μόνους διαμενεῖν.
thought_title: Simple believers and the fire of punishment
pass_a_gloss: From what has been said it is clear to those hearing more intelligently (συνετώτερον) how one must meet (ἀπαντητέον) also the: 'all the other race will be roasted through, but they alone will remain.' It is not wonderful (θαυμαστόν) if such things have been conceived (νενόηκε) by 'the' among us named by the Word 'foolish things (μωρά) of the world' and 'low-born (ἀγενῆ)' and 'despised (ἐξουδενωμένα)' and 'things not being', which 'through the foolishness (μωρίας) of preaching (κηρύγματος) God was pleased (εὐδόκησεν) to save, those believing in him, since in the wisdom of God the world through wisdom did not know God'; not able to articulate (διαρθρῶσαι) the matters of the passages (τόπους) nor having wished to give leisure (σχολάσαι) to the searching (ἐρεύνῃ) of the Scripture, though Jesus says 'search (ἐρευνᾶτε) the Scriptures'; and they have supposed (ὑπείληφε) such things about the fire brought on by God and about the things that will befall those who have sinned. And perhaps, as it suits children that some things be said suitable (κατάλληλα) to their infancy (νηπιότητι), toward turning (ἐπιστρέφειν) them as quite infant children to the better, so for those whom the Word named foolish of the world and low-born and despised the ready (πρόχειρος) interpretation (ἐκδοχή) about punishments (κολάσεων) fits, they not having room for (χωροῦσιν) other turning (ἐπιστροφήν) than that through fear and imagination (φαντασίας) of punishments and abstention (ἀποχήν) from many evils. The Word therefore says that only those will remain untasting (ἀγεύστους) of the fire and the punishments who have been utmost (ἄκρως) purified (κεκαθαρμένους) in doctrines (δόγματα), habits (ἤθη) and the ruling faculty (ἡγεμονικόν); but those not such, according to worth (ἀξίαν) needing the economy (οἰκονομίας) of punishment through fire, it says will be in these for some end (ἐπί τινι τέλει), which it befits God to bring on those made 'according to the image' of him and having lived against the will (βούλημα) of the 'according to the image' nature. And these things too against the: 'all the other race will be roasted through, but they alone will remain.'

choices.english: can take in no other way
choices.why: οὐ χωροῦσιν: 'have no room for' changed to 'can take in no other way'; τῶν πολλῶν κακῶν now 'their many evils'; φαντασίας 'picture' changed to 'imagining'
διαμενεῖν: 'remain' changed to 'survive' to match Celsus's quoted verb in the same chapter

pass_b_english: From what has been said it is clear, to those who listen with more understanding, how one must answer also his words, “all the rest of the race will be roasted through, while they alone will survive.” It is no wonder if such ideas have been formed by those among us whom the Word calls “the foolish things of the world”, “the low-born”, “the despised” and “the things that are not” (1 Corinthians 1:27–28), those whom “through the foolishness of preaching God was pleased to save”, namely “those who believe” in him, “since in the wisdom of God the world through wisdom did not know God” (1 Corinthians 1:21). They are not able to set out clearly the sense of the passages, nor have they been willing to give their time to searching the Scripture, although Jesus says, “Search the Scriptures” (John 5:39); and so they have formed such notions about the fire that God brings on and about what will happen to those who have sinned.

And perhaps, just as it suits children to be told certain things fitted to their infancy, so as to turn them, being very young children, toward what is better, so for those whom the Word has named the foolish things of the world, the low-born and the despised, the obvious understanding of the punishments is fitting, since they can take in no other way of turning back and of keeping away from their many evils than through fear and the imagining of the punishments.

The Word, then, says that only those will survive without a taste of the fire and the punishments who have been perfectly purified in their doctrines, their character and the ruling part of their soul. But those who are not such, who according to their deserts need the dispensation of punishment through fire, it says will be in these punishments for some end; an end which it befits God to bring upon those who were made “in his image” (Genesis 1:26–27) and have lived against the purpose of the nature that is “in his image.” This, too, is our answer to the words, “all the rest of the race will be roasted through, while they alone will survive.”
notes: The subject of νενόηκε and ὑπείληφε is the neuter plural 'the foolish things' among us (simple believers), not Celsus; the neuter participles that follow agree with them. 1 Corinthians 1:21 is quoted with its clauses reordered and with 'in him' (αὐτῷ) added; the relative ἅτινα makes the syntax loose, smoothed here with 'namely'. ἐξουδενωμένα is Origen's spelling for the ἐξουθενημένα of 1 Corinthians 1:28. ἡγεμονικόν (the Stoic 'ruling faculty') rendered 'the ruling part of their soul'. ἐπί τινι τέλει rendered 'for some end', without deciding whether it means a purpose or a time limit. 'In his image' = Genesis 1:26–27 (κατ᾿ εἰκόνα), cited once. The quoted phrase at the opening and close repeats Celsus's words from 5.14. διαμενεῖν is rendered 'survive' both in Celsus's phrase and in Origen's answer, since Origen turns Celsus's own verb back on him.
Open doubt (review): 5.16: ἐπί τινι τέλει is rendered 'for some end', which leaves open whether Origen means a purpose or a time limit. This is deliberate and noted.
